[![](/assets/blog/avatars/2b97c62c-Arman_photo-300x300.avif)Arman Advani, Director of SEO Strategist at Search Atlas](https://searchatlas.com/blog/author/arman/)[Google Ads](https://searchatlas.com/blog/category/google-ads/)Updated January 26, 20267 min read

Quick answer

## In brief

Google Ads offers broad reach and advanced targeting, while Yelp Ads focus on local searches with simpler setup and high-intent users.

On this page+

When it comes to running PPC campaigns, Google Ads vs. Yelp Ads is a common debate for businesses looking to attract more customers. 🛒

Google Ads is the go-to platform for most advertisers, but Yelp Ads has its own appeal, especially for local businesses wanting to reach people actively searching for services.

Both platforms operate on a pay-per-click model, helping businesses drive traffic and boost sales. But beyond that, they work differently, and choosing the right platform can make a big difference in how effectively you reach your audience.

Advertising in the wrong place could mean wasted budget and missed opportunities. First, we’ll explain what Google Ads and Yelp Ads are, then we’ll show you how to make the most of your choice with [PPC tools](https://searchatlas.com/features/)!

Let’s start! 👇

## What is Google Ads?[](https://searchatlas.com/blog/google-ads-vs-yelp-ads/#what-is-google-ads)

![google ads dashboard example](/static/google-ads-dashboard-example-1024x491-4ba730c5.avif "Via Google Ads")Via Google Ads

Google Ads is one of the most powerful PPC platforms, helping businesses reach potential customers at the exact moment they’re searching. It works on a pay-per-click model, meaning you only pay when someone interacts with your ad.

When a user searches for a product or service, Google runs an auction to decide which ads appear. Winning ads show up in search results or across websites, [YouTube](https://searchatlas.com/pt-br/blog/keywords-for-youtube-shorts-2024/), and apps through the Google Display Network.

Businesses can target audiences based on keywords, demographics, and browsing behavior, ensuring ads reach the right people.

Unlike Yelp Ads, which target users browsing local business listings, Google Ads captures demand by putting businesses in front of active searchers.

![Search Atlas Banner Let Smart Ads be your specialist automate ppc campaign](/static/banner-otto-google-ads-3-1024x207-8f9072b0.avif)

### Google Ads Features[](https://searchatlas.com/blog/google-ads-vs-yelp-ads/#google-ads-features)

Google Ads features are designed to help businesses reach their target audience, optimize campaign performance, and control costs through data-driven strategies and automation:

*   **Search and Display Reach:** Ads appear in Google search results and across the Google Display Network, reaching users on websites, apps, and YouTube.
*   **Keyword Targeting:** Businesses can bid on keywords using broad, phrase, or exact match, ensuring ads show up when users search for relevant terms.
*   **Multiple Ad Formats:** Supports search, display, video, shopping, and local service ads, allowing businesses to choose formats that align with their goals.
*   **Local Service Ads:** Ideal for service-based businesses, these ads appear at the top of local search results and operate on a pay-per-lead model.
*   **Detailed Analytics:** Provides insights into ad performance, [engagement](https://searchatlas.com/blog/blog-engagement/), conversions, and audience behavior, helping businesses refine their strategies in real time.
*   **Pay-Per-Click Model:** Advertisers only pay when someone clicks on their ad, with budget controls and bid adjustments to manage spending effectively.

# Using Yelp, Facebook, and Google Review Logos

[Great Content](https://assetlab.us/category/great-content/), [SEO](https://assetlab.us/category/seo/)

Many people ask us whether they can use logos for review platforms for sites like Yelp, Google, and Facebook on their websites to show visitors their great review score. In this post we take some time to look at the rules for each review platform and provide specific guidance and resources you can use to stay within the terms of service for each of them.

## Why This Is A Concern

The reason this is an open question for many businesses is the cost of trademark infringements. When one business uses a trademarked asset of another the owning business can pursue legal action. This can range from a “stop request” to a “cease and desist” to a lawsuit and damages. So, getting this right does matter.

*   Yelp – Yes, Badge also available
*   Google – No, and no badge available
*   Facebook – Yes, Just the “f” version, no badge available
*   Thumbtack – No, Pro and Review badges available

## Can I Use The Yelp Logo

Yelp is one of the most significant business  review platforms online and Yelp reviews are some of the most trusted by potential customers. Here’s what you need to know:

*   **Yes**, you can use the Yelp logo on your website as long as you respect the logo and link to the Yelp page from that image. \[[Source](https://www.yelp.com/brand), 3/4/2018\]
*   There are several rules for the use of the logo that may apply, please read the source for more information

## Can I Use The Google Logo

The short answer is: **No**

The Google logo and Google My Business logo are in high demand from businesses. However, Google does not allow the logo to be used by others without specific written permission. \[[Source](https://www.google.com/permissions/using-the-logo.html), 3/4/2018\]

Also note, as March 2018 there isn’t any way to get a badge that shows the count or rating associated with Google reviews.

## Can I Use The Facebook Logo

**The Facebook “f” can be used** in specific circumstances and in specific ways. The image itself cannot be modified and some uses are not allowed. There are a variety of other brand assets owned by Facebook such as the word-mark, like icon, etc, all of which have rules. \[[Source](https://en.facebookbrand.com/guidelines/brand) 3/4/2018\]

## Can I Use The Thumbtack Logo

Thumbtack is a growing business directory and provides review capability just like these other platforms. It is popular with home services businesses currently and other areas are growing fast.

**Businesses are not allowed to use the Thumbtack logo** however they are allowed to show the Thumbtack Pro badge or the Reviews Badge as long as it is loaded live from Thumbtack with an HTML snippet.

# Yelp vs. Google vs. Facebook Reviews: which should you focus on and why?

If you are handling the marketing for a small business, it can be a challenge to decide where review efforts should be spent.

Written by

AD

**[Amanda DiSilvestro](https://searchenginewatch.com/author/amanda-disilvestro/)**

#### Amanda DiSilvestro

**If you are handling the marketing for a small business, it can be a challenge to decide [where review efforts should be spent](https://searchenginewatch.com/2016/05/19/five-places-your-business-should-source-online-reviews-other-than-google-yelp/).**

We all know that [reviews help SEO](https://searchenginewatch.com/sew/how-to/2436136/the-importance-of-user-reviews-for-local-seo) in a very real way, and why wouldn’t they?

Customers love to see [reviews](https://searchenginewatch.com/2018/08/13/how-to-optimize-your-google-my-business-listing/) when they are going to select a new business for the first time. In fact, 83% of buyers claim that they no longer trust advertising, but most trust recommendations from [users](https://searchenginewatch.com/2018/12/21/guide-google-analytics-confusing-terms/) online (according to Local Vox citing Formstack).

The SEW newsletter

## Smart marketers know what to read_._

Join search marketers who turn to SEW for important news, useful research and independent analysis. Delivered three times a week.

Email address

Watching search since 1996.[Add SEW as a preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=searchenginewatch.com)

Further, according to Search Engine Land, 72% of consumers trust online [reviews](https://searchenginewatch.com/2019/06/10/online-reviews-powerful-seo-weapons/) as much as personal recommendations from real people.

The problem is, there are a lot of review sites out there, and most of them are not set up to have reviews appear on one another.

Yelp, [Google](https://searchenginewatch.com/2019/04/25/whats-it-like-using-duckduckgo-in-2019/), and (increasingly) Facebook, are all platforms that present [customer reviews](https://searchenginewatch.com/2019/06/17/local-seo-guide/), and this presents a unique challenge. Do you ask for reviews on all three sites? Segment the kind of customers you ask for reviews on each? Disregard a platform all together?

The answer is not an easy one. Larger businesses tend to have such a large customer base that reviews on all three sites (and others) just happen and increase over time, but when you are a small business, you want to collect reviews and have an effective online presence.

Let’s look first at the breakdown of each of these platforms, and then discuss differences and information that can help you to make a good decision on where to focus your marketing efforts.

## **Yelp Reviews**

Let’s start with the toughest of the three sites (at least in my personal opinion). Yelp actively discourages its business users from asking for reviews. According to an article by [Practical Ecommerce](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/articles/118051-7-ways-to-get-yelp-reviews-without-violating-its-policies), Yelp was quoted as saying:

> “Let’s face it, most business owners are only going to ask for reviews from their happy customers, not the unhappy ones. Over time, these self-selected reviews create bias in the business listing – a bias that savvy consumers can smell from a mile away.”

![yelp-reviews](https://searchenginewatch.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/25/2016/09/yelp-reviews.png)

Further, if you’ve ever experienced this, you will know that Yelp does not post all of the reviews you get (say what?).

It’s true; they do not post all of your reviews, and for businesses that
